en.stem: State the sign convention for enthalpy change in exothermic and endothermic reactions.
en.answer: An exothermic reaction releases heat and usually has ΔH < 0. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat and usually has ΔH > 0.

en.stem: Why is the enthalpy change of a reaction more useful experimentally than an absolute enthalpy value?
en.answer: The heat transferred under specified conditions can be measured, allowing a difference between final and initial enthalpy to be determined; absolute total enthalpy is not directly measurable in a simple experiment.

en.stem: The enthalpy assigned to reactants for a reaction is 180 kJ and to products is 125 kJ. Find ΔH and interpret its sign.

en.stem: Compare exothermic and endothermic energy profiles using the relative levels of reactants and products.
